images.title: Eleven fourths and eight thirds
images.purpose: Show 11 pieces of 1/4 paratha as 11 jumps on a number line from 0 to 3 landing on 11/4 (2 3/4), and 8 slices of 1/3 pizza as 2 whole pizzas and 2 slices, so 8/3 = 2 2/3.
images.composition: Two bands one above the other: a number line with 11 jumps of 1/4 on top, and 3 pizzas (2 whole and 1 with 2 slices) below, each band with a one-line caption and its result at the right.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816, in two bands split by one thin grey #6B7280 horizontal line at y 390 from x 128 to x 1328. TOP BAND: the caption 11 pieces of 1/4 paratha at the left (dark #1F2937, 40 px, left edge x 128, about y 60) and the result 11/4 = 2 3/4 right-aligned to x 1328 (bold, 60 px, about y 60). One thin dark #2B2B2B number line at y 260 from x 128 to x 1328 with exactly 13 vertical ticks, one every 100 px: 4 tall ticks (44 px) at x 128, 528, 928 and 1328 labelled under the line 0, 1, 2 and 3 (44 px, bold, about y 320), and 9 short ticks (26 px) between them with no labels. Exactly 11 curved arrows (hops), each 100 px wide and about 50 px high, from one tick to the next tick on its right with the arrowhead at the right end, starting at 0 and ending at x 1228: the first 8 hops (0 to 2) teal #0072B2 and the last 3 hops (2 to 2 3/4) reddish purple #CC79A7. A reddish purple dot (24 px) on the line at x 1228 with the label 11/4 above the last hop (bold, 56 px, about y 160). BOTTOM BAND: the caption 8 slices of 1/3 pizza at the left (40 px, left edge x 128, about y 440) and the result 8/3 = 2 2/3 right-aligned to x 1328 (bold, 60 px, about y 440). Three flat round pizzas, each 220 px across with a thin dark outline (3 px), centres at y 620 and x 400, 728 and 1056. PIZZA 1 and PIZZA 2: each cut by 3 thin dark lines from the centre to the edge (at 12, 4 and 8 o'clock) into 3 equal slices, all 6 slices filled teal. PIZZA 3: only 2 slices drawn, the slices from 12 to 4 o'clock and from 4 to 8 o'clock, both filled reddish purple, with the third slice (8 to 12 o'clock) missing and shown only by a thin dashed grey outline of its edges. Under pizzas 1 and 2 a thin grey bracket line (x 290 to x 838, y 745) with the text 2 whole pizzas (36 px, about y 775) centred at x 564; under pizza 3 the text 2 slices left over (36 px, about y 775) centred at x 1056. So 8 slices drawn in all, 6 teal and 2 purple. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
more or fewer than 11 hops, 13 ticks or 8 slices
a pizza slice that is not one third of its pizza
images.takeaway: 11 pieces of 1/4 make 2 whole parathas and 3 pieces of 1/4 over, so 11/4 = 2 3/4; 8 slices of 1/3 make 2 whole pizzas and 2 slices over, so 8/3 = 2 2/3.
images.description: A number line from 0 to 3 with 11 jumps of 1/4 landing on 11/4, and two whole pizzas cut in 3 slices plus a pizza with 2 slices, with 11/4 = 2 3/4 and 8/3 = 2 2/3 written beside them.
images.context: Concept image for Fourths and Thirds Past One Whole. It follows the idea of the figures in your maths book (pieces of 1/4 placed along a number line and a pizza cut into 3 equal slices) and shows the concept's own two examples, 11 pieces of 1/4 paratha and 8 slices of 1/3 pizza.
images.teaching_notes: Make groups of the bottom number: groups of 4 on the line, groups of 3 on the pizzas. The slip to watch is counting the leftover as a new whole: 3 pieces of 1/4 is 3/4, not 3.

image_decisions.why: The 11 hops of 1/4 and the 8 pizza slices in groups of 4 and 3 show how many wholes and how many pieces are left over.
